correctness.rationale: With individually named parameters the complete nonalgebraic singleton types are exactly the distinct labelled one-point order diagrams: finite one-point extensions are realized and homogeneity identifies realizations of the same diagram over the fixed names. For below/above sets L,U the down-set/up-set conditions and L<U are necessary and sufficient for transitivity (strict comparison also ensures disjointness). The two pure cases give 2∏S_ℓ−1. In a mixed case every member of L and U must be on the same chain; positive prefix and suffix lengths summing to grade j give exactly j−1 choices on a chain of size at least j. Thus c₁=2k. At step j≥2 truncating the not-yet-resolved chain factors at j−1 changes the degree-j product coefficient by exactly q_j, the number of lengths ≥j, since each changed factor first differs by z^j and every other factor has constant term one. The mixed contribution is (j−1)q_j, so the coefficient recovers q_j with slope j+1 after subtracting the known baseline. Inductively this determines the counts below r=floor(n/2). For r≥2 the known remaining sum is at most 2r+1; there are at most two lengths ≥r, and a pair must be (r,r) or (r,r+1). For n=2,3 the number of parts suffices, and n=1 has just one profile. The even sharpness profiles have identical q_j below r but Δq_r=−1 and the same degree-r baseline; adding a singleton to both in the odd case preserves the first disagreement and its coefficient. At n=2,3 the grade-zero collision suffices. The totals of the two 17-point examples are both 331 but c₂=12 and 15. A fresh bounded check confirmed direct-extension counts for all 44 profiles through n=7, reconstruction for all 28,628 profiles through n=30, sharpness through n=30, and the scalar collision.
residual_risks: The bounded replay is not an all-n proof; the triangular reconstruction and sharpness arguments establish the infinite statements. Only the chain-length multiset is reconstructed, not the original name assignments or arbitrary finite bases.

value.rationale: This is a natural inverse problem about how much of the type spectrum determines the parameter shape. The result makes exactly the first half of the grades sufficient, gives a constructive inverse, and proves that the last retained grade can be indispensable at every size. The scalar collision shows why merely counting types does not resolve the same problem. The combination is more informative than a routine extension count or a small-sample census.
residual_risks: The inverse requires the base size and the disjoint-chain hypothesis; it is not a result about arbitrary finite posets or bit-complexity optimality.
